name: Reconcile Stripe payouts against NetSuite with Claude and flag exceptions in Slack

parameters.content:
## Reconcile Stripe payouts against NetSuite with Claude and flag exceptions in Slack

Finance teams that match bank feeds, processor payouts and the ledger in spreadsheets every morning.

### How it works
Trigger: Daily run at 6am after bank and processor feeds update; on-demand run before close.
1. Pull the three sides
2. Match deterministically
3. Classify the breaks
4. Explain the unknowns
5. Route for approval
6. Post approved entries
7. Maintain the reconciliation file
8. Close-readiness report
Every AI step is followed by a "Needs a person?" gate that parks low-confidence items; the write-back waits for an approval.

### Setup
1. Open "Config (edit me)" and fill in the fields (names, approver, quiet hours, thresholds).
2. Add credentials: Anthropic, plus NetSuite / Xero / QuickBooks, Stripe / Adyen + Plaid.
3. Run once with test_mode on, read the output, then switch the trigger on.

### Customization tips
Set the matching tolerances and the exception owners in the Config node; swap NetSuite for Xero or QuickBooks.
Guardrail to keep: Nothing posts to the ledger without an accountant's approval; auto-matching only marks, it does not create entries.

Full blueprint: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/financial-reconciliation-automation/

## Trigger and config
The entry point and the one node you edit: names, approver, quiet hours, test mode.

## 1. Pull the three sides
Bank transactions (Plaid or bank API), processor payouts and transaction detail (Stripe, Adyen, PayPal), and ledger entries (NetSuite, Xero, QuickBooks, Sage) for the period

## 2. Match deterministically
Exact matches on amount and reference; one-to-many for processor payouts (payout = sum of transactions − fees − refunds); tolerance matching for FX; each match tagged with the rule that made it

## 3. Classify the breaks
Unmatched items grouped: timing (in transit), fees, refunds, chargebacks, duplicates, unknown

## 4. Explain the unknowns
For remaining breaks the agent reads the descriptions, amounts, dates and nearby transactions and writes the most likely explanation with the evidence — never posting anything

## 5. Route for approval
Proposed entries and explanations to the accountant with approve / edit / investigate buttons; anything above a threshold goes to the controller

## 6. Post approved entries
Approved journal entries posted to the ledger with the match evidence attached; the reconciliation report updated

## 7. Maintain the reconciliation file
A living reconciliation per account: matched, proposed, open, aged — the file auditors ask for, always current

## 8. Close-readiness report
Daily count and value of open breaks by age and type; a red flag when an item passes 5 days unexplained

## Fill this in first
Every later node reads these values. Keep test_mode on for the first week.

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Explain the unknowns" step of the Financial Reconciliation Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: For remaining breaks the agent reads the descriptions, amounts, dates and nearby transactions and writes the most likely explanation with the evidence — never posting anything.

Rules:
- Nothing posts to the ledger without an accountant's approval; auto-matching only marks, it does not create entries.
- The agent explains; it never proposes an amount that is not derivable from the data.
- Every posted entry carries the match evidence and approver for audit.
- Aged open items escalate automatically so nothing hides until close.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

nodes.notes:

nodes.name: Needs a person?
nodes.notes: True = the AI step was not sure or flagged the item → dead letter, a person looks. False = continue. Wire the dead letter to a Slack message or a sheet so nothing fails silently.

nodes.name: Needs a person: Explain the unknowns
nodes.notes: Dead letter. Replace this no-op with a Slack message or a sheet row that carries the raw item and the reason — silent failures are the ones that cost.

nodes.name: Slack approval: Route for approval
nodes.notes:
Route for approval

Proposed entries and explanations to the accountant with approve / edit / investigate buttons; anything above a threshold goes to the controller.

Send-and-wait: the run pauses here until someone presses Approve or Reject. Set config.approver in "Config (edit me)".

nodes.name: Approved?
nodes.notes: True = approved → continue to the write-back. False = rejected → stop here; the item stays where it was.

nodes.name: Rejected: Route for approval
nodes.notes: Rejected by the approver. Nothing is written. Optionally log the rejection to your sheet so the weekly count of corrections is visible.
